# Peru TRAVEL SURVIVAL KIT

**Traveler Types Covered**: Adventure/Culture/Culinary/Solo

## 1. SIM CARD SOLUTIONS

| **Aspect**            | **Details to Find**                                                         |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Providers**         | Claro, Movistar, Entel, Bitel                                              |
| **Price Options**     | 10 PEN (3 days), 20 PEN (7 days), 30 PEN (15 days), 50 PEN (30 days)       |
| **Data Allocation**   | Pre-paid plans usually offer 1.5GB to 10GB depending on the price          |
| **Validity Period**   | 3 to 30 days                                                               |
| **Hotspot/Tethering** | Allowed on most Claro and Entel pre-paid plans                              |
| **Coverage**          | Claro has the best rural/Andean coverage; Entel is excellent in cities      |
| **Where to Buy**      | Official stores (Claro/Movistar) in malls or at the airport (pricier)       |
| **Alternative: eSIM** | Airalo (approx. $9 for 1GB/7 days) or Holafly (Unlimited data packages)     |

**Recommendations**: 
- **Short trips**: Buy a Claro SIM at the airport for convenience, though it costs more than in the city.
- **Longer stays**: Visit an official Entel or Claro store in Miraflores (Lima) with your passport for the best rates.

---

## 2. AIRPORT TRANSFERS

**Route**: From Jorge Chávez International Airport (LIM) to Miraflores/San Isidro

| **Mode**                     | **Duration**       | **Cost**      | **Booking**                    | **Convenience** | **Best For**               |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------- | ------------------------------ | --------------- | -------------------------- |
| **Airport Express Lima**     | 45–60 min          | 30 PEN ($8)   | Online or at the bus counter   | Excellent       | Solo travelers, safety     |
| **Taxi Green/Directo**       | 45–60 min          | 60–80 PEN     | Inside terminal counter        | Very Good       | Families, groups, safety   |
| **Cabify / Uber**            | 45–70 min          | 40–60 PEN     | App-based                      | Good            | Familiarity, price         |
| **Local Combi/Bus**          | 90+ min            | 2–5 PEN       | On the street outside          | Poor            | Extreme budget, no luggage |

**Boarding Location**: Official taxis and buses are located immediately outside the customs exit. For ride-hailing apps, use the designated "App Pickup" zone in the parking lot.

---

## 3. CURRENCY EXCHANGE

**Current Exchange Rate**: 1 USD = ~3.75 PEN (Sol)

| **Location**        | **Why It's Best**          | **Address**                      | **Hours**       | **Rates**       | **Tips** |
| ------------------- | -------------------------- | -------------------------------- | --------------- | --------------- | -------- |
| **Jr. Ocoña**       | Historical exchange hub    | Jirón Ocoña, Central Lima        | 9 AM - 6 PM     | Best in city    | High competition |
| **Money Changers**  | Street changers (vests)    | Main squares (Miraflores)        | Daylight hours  | Market rate     | Safe and fast    |
| **Western Union**   | Reliable branch exchange   | Various locations (Larco Ave)    | 9 AM - 8 PM     | Fair            | Bring passport   |

**Universal Tips**: Avoid airport exchanges as rates are 10-15% worse. Always check for the "BCRP" watermark on bills to avoid counterfeits, which are common in Peru.

## 5. MUST-TRY FOODS

🍽️ **Ceviche** – Seafood
→ What: Raw fish marinated in lime juice, chilies, and onions.
→ Where: La Mar (Lima) or any local "Cevicheria."
→ Price: 30–70 PEN.
→ Try with: Leche de Tigre and a cold beer.

🍽️ **Lomo Saltado** – Stir-fry
→ What: Beef strips sautéed with soy sauce, onions, tomatoes, and fries.
→ Where: Gastón Acurio restaurants or local "Menus."
→ Price: 25–50 PEN.
→ Try with: White rice (always served together).

🍽️ **Cuy Chactado** – Traditional Andean
→ What: Whole fried guinea pig.
→ Where: Specialized restaurants in Cusco or Arequipa.
→ Price: 60–90 PEN.
→ Try with: Rocoto Relleno (stuffed spicy pepper).

## 7. SUPERMARKETS & CONVENIENCE STORES

- **Wong**: Upscale, excellent deli and imported goods. Best for high-quality produce.
- **Metro / Plaza Vea**: Standard supermarkets with competitive pricing on essentials.
- **Tambo+**: Ubiquitous convenience store. Best for quick snacks, water, and cheap alcohol.
- **Vivanda**: Boutique grocery shopping, mostly in affluent Lima neighborhoods.

## 10. BEST PUBS & BARS

- **Ayahuasca (Barranco, Lima)**: Set in a converted mansion; famous for macerated Piscos and incredible decor.
- **Museo del Pisco (Cusco/Lima)**: Educational and fun; great for tasting different Pisco varieties.
- **Nuevo Mundo Draft Bar (Lima)**: Best for Peruvian craft beer enthusiasts.
- **Wild Rover (Cusco)**: High-energy backpacker bar if you are looking for a party.

## BONUS SECTIONS

### 11. LOCAL FESTIVALS & EVENTS
Peru hosts vibrant celebrations throughout the year that blend Catholic and indigenous traditions.

| **Festival**      | **Date**       | **Location**   | **What it is** |
| ----------------- | -------------- | -------------- | -------------- |
| **Inti Raymi**    | June 24th      | Cusco          | The Incan Festival of the Sun; massive theatrical performances. |
| **Fiestas Patrias**| July 28-29th   | Nationwide     | Independence Day celebrations with parades and parties. |
| **Lord of Miracles**| October        | Lima           | One of the world's largest religious processions; everyone wears purple. |

### 12. CUSTOMS & ETIQUETTE

#### 12a. Temple & Sacred Site Dress Code
Respect at Incan sites and Catholic cathedrals is paramount.

| **Rule**                | **What to Check**                            | **Enforcement Level**           |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| **Modesty in Churches** | Remove hats; cover shoulders                 | Strict in active cathedrals     |
| **Sacred Incan Stones** | Never touch or sit on Incan stonework        | Extremely strict (guards present)|
| **Pathways**            | Stay on marked trails at Machu Picchu        | Mandatory                       |

#### 12b. The Head, Feet & Body — Cultural Hierarchy
Personal space is smaller than in the West, but respect is shown through physical cues. Avoid pointing with fingers; use a subtle nod of the head instead.

#### 12c. Interaction & Religious Etiquette
Peru is a deeply Catholic country with strong Andean spiritual roots.

| **Rule**                         | **Detail**                                                             | **Who It Applies To** |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| **Church Silence**               | No talking during Mass; no flash photography                           | All visitors          |
| **Pachamama Offerings**          | Respect "Pagos a la tierra" (offerings) found on trails                | Hikers/Trekkers       |

#### 12d. Saving Face & Conflict Resolution
Direct confrontation is usually avoided; a polite, indirect approach is much more effective in Peru. Use "por favor" and "gracias" liberally to maintain social harmony.

#### 12e. Responsible Tourism & Child Welfare
Do not give money to children begging in the streets of Cusco or Lima as it encourages truancy. Instead, support local schools or legitimate NGOs like those listed at "Causas.pe."

#### 12f. General Social Customs & Greetings
Greetings involve a single kiss on the right cheek between women and between men and women. Handshakes are standard for men.

### 13. SAFETY & PRACTICAL INFORMATION

#### 13a. Vaccinations & Preventative Health
Travelers should ensure they are up to date on routine vaccines before visiting.

| **Vaccine / Medication**           | **Priority Level**   | **Notes**                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Yellow Fever**                   | Recommended          | Essential if visiting the Amazon (Iquitos/Madre de Dios)                                            |
| **Typhoid**                        | Recommended          | For those eating street food or visiting rural areas                                                |
| **Altitude Medication**            | Strongly recommended | Acetazolamide (Diamox) for Cusco and the Andes                                                      |

#### 13b. Mosquito-Borne Illness & Insect Protection
Mosquitoes are a concern in the Amazon Basin and northern coastal areas.

| **Disease**      | **Mosquito Type**        | **Peak Risk**               | **Prevention**                                            |
| ---------------- | ------------------------ | --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Dengue**       | Aedes                    | Rainy season (Amazon)       | DEET, long sleeves                                        |
| **Malaria**      | Anopheles                | Low-lying jungle zones      | Prophylaxis for deep jungle travel                        |

#### 13c. Water & Food Safety
Tap water is not potable in Peru and should be avoided for drinking and tooth brushing. Always choose bottled water or use high-quality purification tablets/filters.

#### 13d. Personal Safety & Crime Awareness
Peru is generally safe for tourists, but petty crime and specific scams exist in major cities.

- **ISSUE: Bag-snatching and Pickpocketing**
  **WHERE IT HAPPENS:** Crowded markets (San Pedro in Cusco), busy bus stations, and the historic center of Lima.
  **HOW IT HAPPENS:** Distraction techniques, such as someone spilling something on you or a group creating a sudden commotion.
  **HOW TO AVOID IT:** Wear backpacks on your front in crowds. Use a money belt for passports and large cash amounts. Never hang your bag on the back of your chair in restaurants.
  **WHAT TO DO IF IT HAPPENS:** Report immediately to the *Policía de Turismo* (Tourist Police), who have offices in all major tourist hubs.

- **ISSUE: Express Taxis / Kidnappings**
  **WHERE IT HAPPENS:** Unlicensed taxis hailed from the street, particularly at night in Lima or Arequipa.
  **HOW IT HAPPENS:** The driver picks up an accomplice who robs the passenger or forces them to withdraw money from ATMs.
  **HOW TO AVOID IT:** Never hail a random taxi on the street at night. Use app-based services like Cabify or Uber, or have your hotel/restaurant call a "Taxi de Empresa" (Registered Company Taxi).

- **ISSUE: Counterfeit Currency**
  **WHERE IT HAPPENS:** Small shops, taxis, and street markets.
  **HOW IT HAPPENS:** Sellers may give you fake 10 or 20 Sol bills in your change.
  **HOW TO AVOID IT:** Learn the feel of Peruvian bills. Check for the color-changing ink on the denomination and the watermark. Refuse any bill that looks suspicious or feels "waxy."

- **ISSUE: The "Broken Bird" or Mustard Scam**
  **WHERE IT HAPPENS:** Tourist squares in Lima or Cusco.
  **HOW IT HAPPENS:** Someone "accidentally" drops a substance on your clothes and offers to help clean it off, while an accomplice lifts your wallet.
  **HOW TO AVOID IT:** If someone points out a stain on your clothes, keep walking and clean it yourself in a secure location like your hotel lobby.

#### 13e. Emergency Contacts & Practical Infrastructure
Keep these numbers saved in your phone for your stay in Peru.

| **Service**                            | **Contact**                     | **Notes**                                      |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| **Police Emergency**                   | 105                             | National police line                           |
| **Tourist Police (Lima)**              | (01) 4601060                    | Dedicated English-speaking support             |
| **Ambulance (SAMU)**                   | 106                             | Response times vary by city                    |
| **U.S. Embassy (Lima)**                | (01) 6182000                    | Located in Surco district                      |

### 14. SEASONAL CONSIDERATIONS
- **Dry Season (May–October)**: Best for trekking and Machu Picchu.
- **Wet Season (November–April)**: Expect heavy rain in the Andes; the Inca Trail closes in February.
- **Sun Protection**: The Andean sun is extremely strong due to altitude; high-SPF sunscreen is mandatory.
